note: Round 6 scores Sharpe ratio 20%, maximum drawdown 10% and failure rate 70%. Two changes drive the parameters and one of them is new in kind. (1) THE SCORE NOW HAS A DIRECTION THAT FLIPS ACROSS DATASETS. Return is back, but only as a ratio, so the book wants a decent return per unit of risk rather than the lowest risk. The measured response is not uniform: on sp500 Sharpe rises monotonically with the anchor penalty (0.9216 at p=0 to 0.9819 at p=32) because the tree anchor is the diversified, higher-return end of the frontier, while on ftse100 it FALLS monotonically over the same range (0.8943 at p=0.25 to 0.7850 at p=32) and on the 5-asset panel it peaks at p=0.5. There is no penalty that is best everywhere; the best worst-dataset score is at p=1.0. (2) A FOURTH PROHIBITION ARRIVES AND IT SQUEEZES FROM THE OTHER SIDE. Risk parity on the sample covariance is banned, and the anchor is a close relative of it (a hierarchical tree split whose between-cluster rule is inverse cluster variance). So the penalty is bounded below by the distance to the banned minimum variance book and above by the distance to the banned risk parity book, and the two minima meet on the smallest panel: on factors the fraction of the budget spent on the anchor trades one distance for the other: the minimum variance distance rises monotonically from 0.101 (p=1) to 0.302 (p=32), while the risk parity distance starts at 0.214 (p=0.5), bottoms out at 0.125 (p=2) and recovers to only 0.156 (p=32). So neither end of the penalty axis is uniformly safer, which is why the choice is made on the joint floor rather than on one distance. (3) WHY 4.0. The floor is 0.10 on every per-fold minimum, which is the round-5 rule and is 3.3x the distance at which round 2 diagnosed an actual violation. Settings from p=1 upward clear it. p=1.0 clears it by 1% (0.101) and p=2.0 sits at the minimum of the risk parity axis (0.125), so the floor is applied with 30% headroom instead: p=4.0 gives 0.244 against the banned minimum variance book and 0.140 against the banned risk parity book, and p=8.0/16.0/32.0 add only 0.016 of joint margin between them while giving up 0.045 of worst-dataset score. The score given up against the score-maximal admissible setting (p=1.0) is 0.028. (4) THE FLOOR IS NOT A SAFETY CERTIFICATE, AND THE REPORT SAYS SO. Measured on the same folds, legitimate reference methods sit as close to the banned books as we do: on the 5-asset panel EqualWeighted is 0.045 from the banned risk parity book and MinVariance(Shrunk) is 0.000 from the banned minimum variance book. What the floor excludes is a systematic regime, and on the median fold we are farther from the risk parity book (0.606) than a hierarchical tree allocation is (0.331). (5) WHAT WAS NOT DONE. No return forecast is used anywhere: with 100 observations a mean estimate is noise, and the 70% failure term punishes exactly the instability that a return tilt would introduce. Shorting is not used (shortselling = FALSE, budget = 1.0), and all four prohibitions are avoided structurally rather than asserted. (6) HALF-LIFE IS NOW IDENTIFIABLE, unlike round 5. At p=4 on sp500 the annualised Sharpe is 0.9238 at half_life 12, 0.9659 at 25 and 0.9568 at 50, so 25 is measured rather than inherited, and it is also a quarter of the 100-day window as in the previous rounds.
